forces: No business change may commit for a transaction-critical occurrence that is too large to become durable (#945).
A refusal that can be decided before the business commit must be decided before the commit gate runs, and must name its cause.
Inside the Node binding the event size limit is written once and equals the contract's event_max_bytes.
The frozen Node surface widens only additively: no export changes, and test:exports stays at 19 value and 44 type-only exports (#111, ADR-NODE-001).
Every occurrence at or under the limit keeps the result it gets today, and the contract, the catalog, sdk-core and the HttpDeliveryHandoff interface stay unchanged.
The Node binding gains no generator or drift gate: tests tie the limit to the contract's event_max_bytes (decision 2 of the #945 triage).

security_justification.audit_integrity: An occurrence too large to become durable is refused before the business commit, so the binding no longer lets a transaction-critical change commit with no possible audit record.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: No authentication or authorization logic changes; the class, transaction identifier, commit-state and duplicate refusals keep their meaning and codes.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The occurrence at deliver() is caller-supplied; its serialized size becomes one more checked property of that input, measured by the binding itself and never taken from a caller claim.
security_justification.concurrency: The size check is synchronous and runs inside the existing admission step, before the duplicate check and its reservation, so no await is added and a concurrent duplicate is still refused.
security_justification.confidentiality: The refusal carries a fixed code and the event identifier only, never the occurrence's content or its size; tests use the contract's synthetic example events with padding.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic primitive, hash, signature or key handling is added, removed or changed.
security_justification.error_disclosure: The new code is a fixed literal, and the refusal echoes nothing from the occurrence but its event identifier, read through a guarded read that yields an empty string when it cannot be read.
security_justification.external_security_integration: No transport, exporter, collector or SIEM integration is added; the handoff interface and its result codes are unchanged.
security_justification.fail_posture: The refusal happens before the durability probe, so it can never follow a business commit; today the same input fails only after the commit gate has run.
security_justification.lifecycle: The fixed probe, gate and durability order is unchanged; admission gains one refusal before it, placed after the serialization check and before the snapshot is parsed.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: The binding reads the caller's object once to serialize it and writes nothing to it; edits are confined to the Node binding's source, tests and records, and this change's canonical spec at fold.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No privacy transform, field policy or transformation hook is touched; the check counts bytes and does not inspect or alter content.
security_justification.resource_retention: An oversized input is serialized once and measured, then refused; by design this happens before the frozen snapshot is built, and a refused occurrence is recorded in neither the settled nor the reserved set.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: A redelivered occurrence is measured again at admission; an oversized one is refused every time without running the gate, and a corrected one stays deliverable under the same pair.
security_justification.trust_boundary: An occurrence the host built, copied or reloaded is untrusted input at deliver(); the binding now bounds its size against the contract's limit before doing any further work on it.
